score_formula: Score = completion × relative difficulty / 100. Every planned set has equal weight: an unperformed set contributes zero. For example, completing 75% of sets at 120% of reference effort gives 90 points. Scores can exceed 100.
score_pace_formula: For timed distance, reps or calories: quantity ratio × square root of pace ratio. The pace multiplier is capped at 1.5. Half the distance at the same pace earns half the points; going fast over a very short distance cannot earn full points.
score_limits: Relative difficulty describes measured effort, not perceived exertion, technique or health. Without targets or history, initial values calibrate the reference. Earlier scores are kept separately; only completed sessions without a score can be repaired. Statistics dates are grouped in UTC.
score_volume_formula: Relative difficulty compares each performed set with its reference: reps, distance or duration; with weight, quantity × (kg + 1); with assistance, reps / (assistance kg + 1). Completion counts confirmed sets; a reduced quantity also reduces relative difficulty.
score_legacy: Historical score — previous formula: average exercise performance compared with the first baseline session (100 points). Kept separate from new scores that include completion.
score_reference_policy: Each measurement uses its target as a reference, otherwise suggested previous results, otherwise the initial performed values. References stay fixed for the same program, exercises, order and set counts. Unknown fields are filled on first performance; skipped sets never establish a zero reference.
score_reference_pending: Reference to be established on first performance
